clue.text: Squash lemons with gravity

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, as in 'a face with gravity'

indicators.note: squashing something crushes it out of shape, so the next word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: crush some lemons, perhaps with a weight on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' reads as a drink or a verb about fruit; here it only signals the rearrangement of LEMONS into SOLEMN.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means serious and grave in manner, which is what having gravity describes.

clue.text: Plan to turn up huge pastries?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: mega means huge
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: A scheme for some enormous pastries to appear, as if planning a bakery surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: MEGA TARTS read from bottom to top gives STRATAGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or cunning plan for getting the better of someone.

clue.text: Dance in place, for some souls

blocks.note: first meaning: a party dance of bending backwards under a lowered bar
second meaning: in Catholic theology, the border region of the afterlife for souls such as unbaptised infants

explanation.surface: Dancing on the spot, with a hint at the spiritual fate of some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dance in place' reads as a phrase; 'in' is only the join between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the Caribbean bar-dancing game and the theological border state between heaven and hell.

clue.text: Dessert regimen is disrupted, eating that last bite of gateau

indicators.note: the last bite of something is its final piece, so take the end letter
something disrupted is thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder
the final letter of gateau

explanation.surface: A dieter's plan falling apart over a mouthful of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement uses all of REGIMEN plus the one letter it is said to be eating; gateau ends in U, not E.
explanation.definitionFit: Meringue is a dessert of whipped egg whites and sugar baked until crisp.

clue.text: Between south and north, fly a little bit

indicators.note: says the middle piece sits flanked by the two compass points, one at each end

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a midge is a small flying insect
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: An insect flitting across a map from bottom to top, travelling only a short way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb; it is the insect, a MIDGE, set between S and N to give SMIDGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a tiny amount, an informal word for a very small quantity.

clue.text: Supreme Council of the Armed Forces conceding defeat — or support

blocks.clueFragment: Supreme Council of the Armed Forces
blocks.note: SCAF was the acronym of the military council that ruled Egypt in 2011-12
a player folding gives up, conceding defeat

explanation.surface: A news item about Egypt's ruling generals giving up power, or else backing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Supreme Council of the Armed Forces ran Egypt after Mubarak fell; its initials, SCAF, start the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Scaffolding is a temporary framework that supports workers and materials on a building.

clue.text: Stylish nanny at first engrossed by chubby baby

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it
something engrossed is absorbed into another, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: in means fashionable
chubby means fat
the opening letter of nanny

explanation.surface: A fashionable nanny captivated by a plump little baby in her charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chubby baby' reads as one phrase, but chubby is wordplay and baby alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a very young child, another word for a baby.

clue.text: The Nation's note covering a feeble letter from Greece's uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards
in a down entry, a piece covering another sits on top of it

blocks.note: taken as written
a feeble excuse is a lame one
tau is the Greek letter T
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A political-sounding line about this magazine's comment on a Greek revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: The Nation is the magazine that runs this puzzle, but read plainly it is any country. A LAME TAU goes upwards under G.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American country, so it is literally a nation.

clue.text: No stringed instruments make powerful weapons

blocks.note: N is short for no, as on a yes/no form
ukes is short for ukuleles

explanation.surface: A pacifist slogan suggesting guitars and ukuleles are a better weapon than bombs.
explanation.walkthrough: N plus UKES gives NUKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Nukes is informal for nuclear weapons, the most destructive arms there are.

clue.text: Notice someone from Seinfeld coming back

indicators.note: something coming back travels the opposite way, so the name is read from right to left

blocks.note: Cosmo Kramer is Jerry's neighbour in the sitcom Seinfeld

explanation.surface: Spotting a familiar sitcom character making a return appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: KRAMER read backwards gives REMARK.
explanation.definitionFit: To remark is to notice or observe something, as in 'remark on the change'.

clue.text: BA for soccer player

blocks.note: surface reading: an abbreviation, a university degree or an airline
setter's reading: these two letters are what is left of a four-letter word for the rear when it is cut in two

explanation.surface: A graduate's degree standing in for a footballer, as if qualifications picked the team.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is literally half of BACK, so the clue describes a HALFBACK; it is a reverse clue, where the answer's wordplay leads to the letters shown.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfback is a player positioned between the forwards and the defenders in soccer and other field games.

clue.text: God: new or ancient character?

blocks.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A question of whether a deity is a newcomer or one of the old cast of characters.
explanation.walkthrough: THOR plus N gives THORN, the runic letter þ that Old English used for the 'th' sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorn is an old letter of the runic and Old English alphabets, so it is literally an ancient written character.

clue.text: They break the rules relating to electric guitars

blocks.note: of can mean concerning or relating to
Fender is a famous maker of electric guitars

explanation.surface: Rock guitarists cast as rule-breakers, a nod to the rebellious image of electric guitar music.
explanation.walkthrough: OF plus FENDERS gives OFFENDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenders are people who commit offences, breaking laws or regulations.

clue.text: Work briefly with the left on solidarity and chance for progress

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it in order

blocks.note: op is the short form of opus, a musical work
port is the left-hand side of a ship
solidarity is unity of purpose

explanation.surface: A union slogan: work with the political left in solidarity and you get a chance to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The left' sounds political; here it is the nautical left, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: An opportunity is an opening or favourable moment that lets someone move forward.

clue.text: Loudly ride fast, either north or south — that's one way to find out what people are thinking

definitions.text: one way to find out what people are thinking

indicators.note: done loudly means spoken out, so the words are judged by their sound rather than their spelling

blocks.note: to gallop is to ride a horse at full speed
the North and South Poles are the two poles

explanation.surface: A noisy rider tearing towards one end of the earth, then a claim about reading minds.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are sound-alikes: gallop and pole, spoken, give GALLUP and POLL. Gallup is a US polling company.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gallup poll is an opinion survey, a sampling of the public to learn its views.

clue.text: Favor playing sexy and fast

blocks.note: to favor something is to like it
an actor playing a part appears as that character
hot is slang for sexy

explanation.surface: Preferring to play it sexy and fast, like a racy performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives AS, as in 'playing as' a character.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for very quickly or without hesitation, so it works as an adverb.

clue.text: Mineral found in most alcohol

indicators.note: found in says the answer is lying inside the following words, spanning their join

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A claim that some mineral turns up in nearly every alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: mos(T ALC)ohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral, magnesium silicate, ground to make talcum powder.

clue.text: Tech lover disassembled vehicle

indicators.note: something disassembled is taken apart, so its letters can be put together again in a different order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A gadget enthusiast who took a car apart to see how it worked.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TECH LOVER gives CHEVROLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevrolet is an American car brand, so a Chevrolet is a motor vehicle.

clue.text: Ram a lousy Ford model that's apt to catch fire

blocks.note: bum is American slang for worthless or lousy

blocks.clueFragment: Ford model that's apt to catch fire
blocks.note: the 1970s Ford Pinto became notorious for fuel tanks that could ignite in rear-end crashes

explanation.surface: Driving into a notoriously unsafe Ford car, which may then go up in flames.
explanation.walkthrough: BUM plus PINTO gives BUMP INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram is to collide with something, and to bump into is to strike it while moving.

clue.text: Manufacture inside West Bank, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it
inside says one piece is placed within the other piece

blocks.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so West suggests her first name
the final letter of bank

explanation.surface: Factories being built within the occupied West Bank, put tersely like a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Bank' reads as the territory, but the words are split: West is Mae West, and the last letter of Bank goes inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: To make is to produce or build something, the everyday verb for manufacturing.

clue.text: Drawings I curate after changing sides, put into words

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so an R in the words is swapped for an L

blocks.note: drawings are works of art
taken as written
taken as written, then its R becomes L

explanation.surface: A gallery curator describing how they hang drawings after switching which walls they use.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) and L (left) are the sides: CURATE becomes CULATE, giving ART + I + CULATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate is to express an idea clearly in speech or writing.

clue.text: Texting: "Are you wearing leather in a winter sport setting?"

indicators.note: a body wearing clothes is wrapped in them, so the leather goes around the other piece

blocks.note: leather is animal skin
in text-message shorthand, are you is written RU

explanation.surface: A text message asking whether someone is dressed in leather out on the snow.
explanation.walkthrough: The texting shorthand RU goes inside SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a marked slope for skiing, the place where that winter sport happens.

clue.text: Fifty in rear, fifty in front of retreating antelope with disease

indicators.note: in places the first numeral within the word for a person's rear
in front of says the second numeral is set just before the next piece
retreating means going backwards, so the animal's name is read the other way

blocks.note: the back is the rear of something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L again, the Roman numeral
the gnu, or wildebeest, is an African antelope

explanation.surface: A sick antelope backing away, described in a jumble of numbers like a field report.
explanation.walkthrough: B(L)ACK then L then GNU backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Black lung is pneumoconiosis, a lung illness coal miners get from inhaling coal dust.

clue.text: Herb is a man's name

blocks.note: first meaning: an aromatic culinary plant
second meaning: a male first name

explanation.surface: Herb, short for Herbert, is a man's name; the statement is true on the surface too.
explanation.walkthrough: On the surface Herb is a man's name; but read as the plant, a herb is basil, also a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is both a fragrant kitchen plant and a traditional masculine given name.

clue.text: First of tailors interrupts Lord Wimsey, e.g.

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the next word
something that interrupts breaks into the middle of what follows

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
the opening letter of tailors

explanation.surface: A tailor cutting in on Dorothy L. Sayers' aristocratic detective, perhaps at a fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord does double duty: it gives PEER, and in the surface it is part of the title Lord Peter Wimsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Peter Wimsey's first name is Peter, so he is an example of someone so named.

clue.text: Tatum mysteriously clutching belly

indicators.note: words clutching something hold it tightly within them, spanning their join

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An actor named Tatum oddly gripping his stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mysteriously' looks like an anagram signal; it is only the source of the last letters: ta(TUM MY)steriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Tummy is an informal, childlike word for the belly or stomach.

clue.text: Sandwich covered with salsa and guacamole, flipped in a ball

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the condiment word is read backwards
something covered with a topping is wrapped by it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: a hero is an American name for a long submarine sandwich
salsa and guacamole are both dips served with chips

explanation.surface: A Tex-Mex sandwich loaded with toppings and then flipped while being rolled into a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwich' looks like the verb, but it is the noun; a hero is the American long sandwich. Only the dips are flipped, not the sandwich inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A spheroid is a body shaped like a sphere, so a ball is one.

clue.text: Paint error — to wit, leaving a piece off the end

indicators.text: leaving a piece off the end
indicators.note: dropping a piece from the end removes the final letter of the phrase's word

blocks.note: E is the baseball scorer's abbreviation for an error
to wit and namely both mean that is to say

explanation.surface: A decorator admitting a mistake: a bit of paint missed at the end of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus NAMELY without its Y gives ENAMEL. The E for error is from baseball box scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy kind of paint that dries hard.

clue.text: Hidden quality of inverted mesh in frilly surrounding

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down or back to front, so the word is reversed
surrounding says one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: frilly trimmings are lacy
a net is a mesh

explanation.surface: Something about a mesh fabric turned inside out in frilly lingerie hints at a concealed charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' here belongs to the definition, not a signal to look inside the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Latency is the state of being present but not yet active or visible, a dormant property.

clue.text: Old Testament in Russian? No! Later, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the first piece is placed inside the word that follows

blocks.note: nyet is Russian for no
OT is the usual abbreviation for the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Asked whether the Old Testament exists in Russian, someone refuses, then suggests perhaps later.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation set up the Russian word for no as a piece of the answer rather than a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet means not now but possibly at some future time, so it postpones rather than refuses.
